Deploying C in the reference version succeeds and initializes owner to msg.sender, whereas in the buggy version the constructor reverts, so the deployment itself fails, causing c to be uninitialized/null, and reading c.owner() reverts in the test — but we catch that with try/catch and assert that the transaction succeeded.

After deploying, the reference contract constructor succeeds, making owner == the deployer; the buggy version reverts in constructor, so owner remains address(0); an onlyOwner call succeeds on reference but reverts on buggy version, and we catch that revert.
After constructor, call owner() getter; reference returns msg.sender, second version returns address(0).
setOwner with msg.sender as owner returns true in the reference but false in the buggy version.
After the owner calls setOwner, the reference contract changes owner to the passed address, while the buggy version always resets owner to address(0).

With the owner calling setOwner to transfer ownership to a new address, the reference version succeeds and returns true, while the buggy version reverts because the onlyOwner modifier incorrectly requires the caller not to be the owner.
setOwner succeeds and changes owner; modified version reverts in onlyOwner due to extra revert(), so setOwner fails.

After setOwner is called by the owner, the reference version keeps the new owner, but the buggy version changes the owner back to msg.sender after the modifier body executes, so the owner is the caller instead of the intended new owner.
After owner calls setOwner(0xdeadbeef), the owner getter returns the new address in the reference, but the buggy modifier changes it back to msg.sender, so the assertion fails.
